page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server provisioned within the Bare Metal NVMe product line. The platform is powered by an eight-core, sixteen-thread AMD EPYC 4345P processor operating at a 3.9 GHz base clock on the x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration includes 64 GB of system RAM, providing 4 GB per logical thread. Fast local persistence is integrated directly via a bundled 3890 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address without virtualized hypervisor overhead.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded compute efficiency alongside balanced throughput. The server registers top-decile results in Geekbench single-core testing (3291.0), stress-ng single-core (4645.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (50.25 GB/sec), driven by high core clocks and AVX-512 instruction support. Multi-threaded metrics align within the middle 50% tier, shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11684.0 and PassMark CPU score of 38348.42. The memory subsystem delivers a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3475.43 and cached read throughput of 2099.39 GB/sec, although large-block uncached write bandwidth settles at a lower 24.43 GB/sec.

The qualitative hardware balance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding bare-metal predictability and rapid storage I/O without the pricing premium of massive multi-socket nodes. Because the host integrates nearly 3.9 TB of direct NVMe capacity alongside top-tier per-core CPU performance, it avoids hypervisor virtualization penalties and noisy-neighbor interference.

This hardware composition is well suited for transactional database servers, high-frequency web serving, continuous integration builds, and latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks. It also functions effectively for lightweight machine learning inference, where small language models leverage the high clock speed to achieve text generation rates reaching 451.94 tokens per second.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal instance powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor delivering 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads at 3.9 GHz. Accompanied by 64 GB of system memory and 3890 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage, this x86_64 server eliminates virtualization layers to maximize deterministic throughput. Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 3291.0 and 50.25 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression, alongside average multi-core metrics including a 38348.42 PassMark CPU rating. While large-block memory writes show lower relative throughput, the platform excels in memory caching, fast local I/O, and small-model inference. This makes the server an efficient choice for database operations, backend web serving, compilation pipelines, and latency-sensitive business applications.
